headings.title: Diagnostic console data and lifecycle flows

html:
Diagnostic console data and lifecycle flows

The Console runs as a separate web process so process observations can remain available when the main Agent event loop is slow. It combines local OS/GPU samples with best-effort main-server packets, then exposes cached snapshots and suggested checks. It owns neither task execution nor recovery authority. A displayed request, stage or resource measurement is an observation, not proof of an operation's result.

For operator interpretation, see Errors and diagnostics. Server lifecycle owns listener startup, TLS and login; Observability owns pipeline event projection. Gateway GPU operations have their own GPU guide: the Console samples its local host.

Owners and data sources

flowchart TD Stores[Main run/task summaries and threads] --> Heartbeat[Thread heartbeat] Loop[Main asyncio scheduling] --> Probe[Loop lag probe] HTTP[Main HTTP response creation] --> Timing[Timing middleware] Caller[Explicitly attached pipeline sink] -.-> Projection[Log-policy projection and bounds] Heartbeat --> UDP[Process-identified UDP envelopes] Probe --> UDP Timing --> UDP Projection --> UDP UDP --> Collector[Sidecar collector and target filter] OS[Target process and host OS] --> Sampler[Sidecar sampling worker] GPU[Local NVIDIA CSV query] --> Sampler Collector --> Cache[Sample/event rings and latest-state maps] Sampler --> Cache Cache --> Snapshot[Cached snapshot and deterministic findings] Snapshot --> Portal[Authenticated sidecar HTTP API] Portal --> Browser[Polling page and charts]
Source owner Responsibility
publisher.py Thread/loop heartbeats, HTTP timing, optional pipeline sink, UDP envelope and main-process stack handler.
collector.py IPv4 UDP receive loop, JSON-object decoding and delivery to the sampler.
sampler.py Target identity, OS samples, retained observations, stack requests and snapshot projection.
gpu.py Fixed local NVIDIA query, timeout, failure backoff and device aggregates.
diagnosis.py Pure threshold/stage heuristics and ranked next checks.
app.py Sidecar lifespan, cached HTTP/SSE routes, static assets, branding and login integration.
console.js Coalesced polling, literal-text rendering, chart gaps and explicit stack action.
package exports Publisher exports and lazy application-factory import without worker startup.

The main application exposes console_event_sink on app.state. The current default native request context installs AgentTraceSink; it does not automatically add that console sink. Pipeline stage hints therefore require a caller that explicitly supplies it. The observability context builder accepts explicit sinks. Heartbeat and HTTP publication have their own integration and do not depend on a pipeline sink being attached.

Startup and resource lifetime

sequenceDiagram participant Bundle as Web bundle participant Main as Main API participant Diag as Diagnostics participant App as Sidecar app participant Workers as Sampler / collector Bundle->>Main: Launch API listener Bundle->>App: Set target PID to API child and launch console par Main startup Main->>Diag: Controller lifespan starts diagnostics Diag->>Diag: Register optional SIGUSR2 handler Diag->>Diag: Start thread heartbeat and asyncio probe and Sidecar startup App->>Workers: Sidecar lifespan starts both workers Workers->>Workers: Sample target and bind UDP in receiver thread end Note over App,Workers: Starting the thread is not a UDP readiness acknowledgement Bundle->>App: Signal sidecar termination Bundle->>Main: Signal main termination App->>Workers: Stop collector, close socket, then stop sampler Main->>Diag: Cancel probe, join heartbeat and close resources Note over Bundle,Diag: Reverse-order termination signals precede reaping<br/>each app owns its cleanup concurrently

The web bundle normally starts Console when AOR_CONSOLE_AUTOSTART is enabled. It passes the API child PID to the console environment. The sidecar factory creates workers; its lifespan starts them. The main controller starts diagnostics after restoration/reconciliation reaches background-service startup. A console page can therefore have process samples before any main heartbeat arrives.

The direct CLI console command accepts --target-pid, --host and --port. Supply the running Agent PID when inspecting another process: omitting it selects the console process itself. Starting a standalone console does not install a stack handler in an arbitrary target.

Configuration Checked-out behavior
AOR_CONSOLE_TARGET_PID Target PID for the factory; absent means the current process. Explicit factory/CLI arguments take precedence.
AOR_CONSOLE_HOST Publisher destination, default 127.0.0.1. Also supplies default navigation host.
AOR_CONSOLE_BIND_HOST Collector bind override, default publisher host. The web bundle separately uses this override or its Server host for the HTTP listener.
AOR_CONSOLE_PORT HTTP/navigation port, default 8015; noninteger environment input falls back in the helper.
AOR_CONSOLE_UDP_PORT UDP port override, otherwise the resolved console HTTP port. TCP and UDP are separate listeners even when numbers match.
AOR_CONSOLE_PUBLISH_ENABLED Main publication defaults on. False suppresses normal publisher sends and diagnostic startup; it does not stop the separate sidecar sampler.
AOR_CONSOLE_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS Default one second. Main heartbeat clamps to at least 0.5 seconds; sidecar sampling clamps to at least 0.25 seconds. Invalid text falls back in the sidecar factory but raises in main diagnostics construction.
AOR_CONSOLE_RING_SECONDS Default 900 seconds; sidecar clamps to at least 30, then allocates at least 30 samples. Actual retained duration also depends on interval and sampling cost.
AOR_CONSOLE_STACK_PATH Shared append-only file, default artifacts/console_stack.log relative to each process working directory. Both sides must refer to the same file.

The bundle shares its TLS choice across listeners. The sidecar installs the portal login boundary; stack POST also requires the ordinary same-origin/CSRF checks. Anonymous health responses are reduced by that boundary. HTTP authentication does not authenticate UDP packets. Console URL construction uses the active certificate protocol; wildcard display hosts are replaced with loopback. Listener configuration and navigation URLs are separate concerns.

Packet ingestion and freshness

sequenceDiagram participant Producer as Main producer participant Publisher as UDP publisher participant Collector as Sidecar collector participant Sampler as Sampler state Producer->>Publisher: Emit kind and payload Publisher->>Publisher: Add sequence, PID, birth time and timestamps alt Encoded packet exceeds 60000 bytes Publisher->>Publisher: Replace payload with truncation marker end Publisher-->>Collector: Send one JSON datagram Note over Publisher,Collector: No acknowledgement, retry or ordering repair Collector->>Collector: Decode JSON object, discard malformed input Collector->>Sampler: record_event(envelope) alt PID or birth time differs from pinned target Sampler->>Sampler: Increment rejected_events and discard else Matching target identity Sampler->>Sampler: Append event and stamp local receipt time Sampler->>Sampler: Update heartbeat, request hint or inflight map end

The sampler captures the target's OS birth time at construction. A missing initial birth time rejects every packet; it is not adopted from a sender. PID/birth checks exclude another controller and stale packets after PID reuse, but are not sender authentication. The collector accepts a JSON object and delegates identity checks; it ignores malformed packets and recorder exceptions. A bind failure ends its thread; it does not retry or change the app's health response to a listener failure.

ConsolePublisher.emit sends synchronously through a lazy UDP socket and catches send/serialization errors into last_error. It provides no durable queue or delivery guarantee. Pipeline events alone pass through the configured LOGS redaction projection and recursive limits before publication: depth five, up to 80 collection entries, 120-character keys and 2,000-character strings. Ordinary heartbeat payloads use their own field limits; they are not automatically passed through that pipeline adapter. Prompt previews and stack text are diagnostic content, not a universal sanitized export.

Thread heartbeats include up to 100 open run summaries, up to 500 queued tasks, slot estimates and Python thread identities. Failed store reads substitute empty lists. These are capped observations; they are not the full task queue or a transactionally consistent controller snapshot. HTTP timing ends when call_next produces a response; it does not measure a streaming body's lifetime.

main.status becomes connected after any accepted heartbeat and stays so even when that heartbeat ages. Read thread_heartbeat_age_ms and event_loop_heartbeat_age_ms for freshness. Ages use local receipt time; sequence numbers do not deduplicate or reorder packets. The latest arriving heartbeat replaces active summaries. Pipeline hints are retained separately and merged into the displayed request list, so an event-only entry need not still be active.

Sampling, retention and diagnosis

flowchart TD Tick[Sampler worker tick] --> Process[Read target with psutil] Process --> Valid{Target reads available?} Valid -->|Yes| Metrics[CPU, memory, threads, I/O and host pressure] Valid -->|No| Missing[Missing-process observation] Metrics --> Retry{GPU retry time reached?} Missing --> Retry Retry -->|No| Absent[Unavailable GPU values] Retry -->|Yes| Query[Fixed nvidia-smi query with 0.75 second timeout] Query --> Devices{Usable devices returned?} Devices -->|Yes| Aggregate[UUID records, max utilization and combined VRAM] Devices -->|No| Backoff[Clear GPU readings and delay retry 30 seconds] Backoff --> Absent Aggregate --> Ring[Append combined sample to ring] Absent --> Ring Ring --> Read[Cached snapshot request] Read --> Rules[Threshold and stage heuristics] Rules --> Findings[At most eight ranked findings with next checks]

Process samples include target CPU/RSS/memory share, handles/connections, up to eight threads ranked by CPU-time delta, nonnegative I/O deltas and host pressure. The first CPU/thread observation establishes a baseline. A psutil access failure in the guarded reads can produce status: missing even without proof that the process exited. Diagnosis's process_down wording must be interpreted alongside target identity and permissions. The worker does not catch every possible provider exception around its outer loop.

GPU sampling uses the shared CSV parser. It rediscovers devices by UUID, leaves unsupported/nonfinite metrics null and keeps observed zero distinct from unavailable. Aggregate utilization is the busiest available device; aggregate VRAM is summed used/total for usable device readings. These are device-wide host values, not memory or compute attributable to the Agent. Missing command, timeout, failed exit or empty devices clears old readings and backs off for 30 seconds. Sampling continues independently of whether the target process is present. Snapshot requests never invoke nvidia-smi.

The sample ring uses the configured capacity, the event ring retains 2,000 records and the stack-result ring retains ten. API series/GPU history contain at most 180 points, recent events at most 120 and merged requests at most 100. These limits do not bound every map: per-request pipeline hints have no expiry here, and a lost HTTP finish packet can leave an inflight key. A sidecar restart clears these RAM observations. The stack file is separate and append-only; these modules provide no file rotation or durable telemetry replay.

Diagnostic rule Evidence used
Missing process Latest sample reports missing; returned immediately as the only finding.
Stale main heartbeat Thread heartbeat age exceeds 10 seconds.
Blocked event loop Thread heartbeat is younger than 4 seconds while loop heartbeat exceeds 4 seconds. No prior loop heartbeat means this rule cannot establish blockage.
CPU / memory pressure Target CPU at least 85%, or target memory share at least 80%.
Run slots occupied Nonzero parallel limit, active count at/above it and no available slots.
Model / execution hint First matching retained request stage/event; severity increases at 30 seconds of request age, not measured stage duration.
Slow route Maximum among the latest 20 retained route durations reaches 3 seconds.
No clear bottleneck No preceding rule matches the available observations.

Findings are sorted by severity and kind, then limited to eight. They launch no model call, tool, restart or task control. “No clear bottleneck” means the current observations did not match these rules; it does not certify system health.

Browser reads and optional stream

sequenceDiagram participant Page as Browser / API client participant Auth as Portal boundary participant API as Console API participant Cache as Sampler cache loop One-second browser timer or manual Refresh alt Read already pending Page->>Page: Await existing promise without another fetch else No pending read Page->>Auth: GET /api/console/snapshot Auth->>API: Admit authenticated read API->>Cache: snapshot() Cache-->>API: Cached measurements and findings API-->>Page: JSON Page->>Page: Render once and clear pending promise end end opt Separate client chooses SSE Page->>Auth: GET /api/console/stream Auth->>API: Admit stream loop Sampler interval API->>Cache: snapshot() API-->>Page: Named snapshot event end end Note over API,Cache: Neither read path samples hardware

The bundled page polls; it does not open an EventSource. A pending promise coalesces overlapping timer/manual reads. Manual reads use the shared busy display, and errors use the shared error presenter. Cards use text nodes rather than interpreting diagnostic values as HTML. The page shows the most recent 40 events. Charts take the latest 120 points, align by timestamps, clamp drawing to 0–100% and break the path at missing/nonfinite values. Process CPU itself can exceed 100% on a multicore host; the chart scale is a display limit.

/healthz reports sidecar availability plus cached details for an authenticated owner. It does not prove UDP binding, heartbeat freshness or sampler progress. Use sample count, generated times, heartbeat ages and actual target observations together. The main Server's console entry page links to this separate listener; reloading that entry cannot restart or repair the sidecar.

Explicit stack capture

sequenceDiagram participant Page as Console page participant API as Authenticated stack route participant Sampler as Sidecar sampler participant Target as Configured target PID participant Log as Shared stack log Page->>API: POST /api/console/stack API->>Sampler: capture_stack() alt SIGUSR2 unavailable Sampler->>Sampler: Build unsupported result else Signal available Sampler->>Log: Record current byte size Sampler->>Target: Send SIGUSR2 alt Signal delivery fails Sampler->>Sampler: Build failed result else Signal delivered to a configured handler Target->>Log: Append all-thread Python dump Sampler->>Log: Poll for growth for up to 1.5 seconds Log-->>Sampler: New text, if available Sampler->>Sampler: Build captured or timeout result end end Sampler->>Sampler: Retain result in ten-entry stack ring Sampler-->>API: Return retained result API-->>Page: Result text/status Page->>API: Refresh cached snapshot

Capture is intended for the main Agent that successfully registered its faulthandler handler. It sends a real OS signal. The sidecar does not verify that registration or recheck the target birth time before signalling, so a manually chosen arbitrary/reused PID is not a supported substitute for the configured main process. Disabling main publication also skips automatic handler registration. On unsupported platforms it returns unsupported; delivery errors return failed; no appended output before the deadline returns timeout. File-access failures can still propagate through the HTTP error boundary.

The reader returns the last 24,000 characters of the newly appended text and keeps the result in RAM. It polls every 50 milliseconds while waiting. A busy indicator in the page does not deduplicate stack requests, and no lock serializes captures; concurrent captures can observe overlapping output. Capturing a stack neither stops a task nor changes its permission, completion or recovery state.

Verification boundaries

Existing console tests exercise rings, synthetic findings, event merging, HTTP assets and bounded/projected publication. GPU tests supply fake subprocess results for topology, null readings, backoff, recovery and cached reads. Controller optimization tests cover rejection of another PID/process birth. The browser fixture serves fake snapshots for device replacement, unavailable states and chart gaps. Those checks do not establish delivery under UDP loss, successful real-target signal handling, driver installation or complete coverage of every diagnostic threshold.
